findings.source_quote: ὡς ἐν πολλῷ τῷ χρόνῳ ὑποκειμένης ἕως φυσικῆς ὑποζέουσα ἡ θερμότης
findings.english_quote: as it lay beneath over a long period, until natural, the heat simmering underneath
findings.issue: The draft openly acknowledges the difficulty, but this fragment does not provide a defensible English construction conveying the supplied sequence. Listing possible word equivalents is not complete translation coverage. The absence of a following clause after ἕως does not itself establish corruption, since ἕως can also govern a genitive; nevertheless, no contextual interpretation of ἕως φυσικῆς and the surrounding construction is established here. The block concerns unsupported meaning, not merely competing interpretations or an unverified transcription.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep publication blocked pending a defensible grammatical and contextual account of the supplied wording. The proposed replacement of ἕως with ὕλης is a conjectural alteration, not the image-checked reading, and must remain identified as such. Rechecking the same print alone would not resolve the interpretive problem. Any explicitly justified change of source reading and resulting English must undergo fresh review.

findings.issue: Physical mixture is a defensible reading within this natural-philosophical allegory, but the pairing of Aphrodite with generation also strongly supports sexual union. English “mixture” does not readily preserve that sexual sense. No note discloses this material alternative or explains the different rendering of the same noun as “unions” in 6.10.
findings.suggested_revision: Explicitly compare “Aphrodite sexual union and generation” with the current wording. Either adopt a contextually justified rendering of the sexual sense or retain “mixture” with a note preserving “sexual union” as an alternative and explaining the physical reading and the gloss difference from 6.10. The revised text and notes require fresh review.
